purpose: Frozen-policy estimator audit followed by one-update-per-batch RLVR training.

stages.name: acquire
stages.objective: Freeze a finite prompt frame, verifier suites, current and stale checkpoints, and contamination boundaries.
inputs: Versioned math and code prompt identifiers with known target masses
Current-policy, stale-policy, tokenizer, and decoder revisions
Public and hidden verifier source hashes
checks: Prompt support is finite, normalized, and reconstructible
Hidden tests are disjoint from SFT, nuisance, and allocator data
Licenses and sandbox requirements are recorded

stages.name: process
stages.objective: Normalize verifier outcomes and validate exact sampler/scorer probability agreement.
inputs: Temperature-softmax decoder specification and maximum response length
Parser, timeout, sandbox-error, EOS, and truncation reward rules
checks: Sampler frequencies agree with scored masses in finite-vocabulary conformance tests
Prompt and sequence mixture masses normalize in high precision
No verifier outcome is retried or silently dropped

stages.name: build
stages.objective: Construct policy, stale actor, frozen reward/length predictors, prompt baseline, and adaptive proposal.
inputs: Frozen alpha grid, proposal support floor, length target, and dual schedule
checks: Nuisance and proposal models use only prior-iteration disjoint data
Current and behavior scorers share tokenizer, masks, and decoder semantics
Policy and nuisance tensor hashes are frozen before each audit

stages.name: train
stages.objective: Audit projected bias/variance at frozen policies, freeze alpha, then run single-use one-update batches.
inputs: Matched token, verifier-call, hyperparameter, and batch-admission budgets
checks: Every theorem-facing trajectory is generated after iteration choices freeze and has use_count one
The numerical mixture-weight bound and source-specific ESS are checked
Batch admission reserves worst-case cost and reports terminal undershoot

stages.name: evaluate
stages.objective: Aggregate gradient MSE, held-out reward, reward-length frontiers, and deliberate theorem violations.
inputs: Frozen intervals, thresholds, seed pairing, and multiplicity rules
Hidden verifier variants and shuffled/random/anti-correlated controls
checks: Monte Carlo reference uncertainty is propagated
Prefix reuse and repeated replay are labeled as different or biased objectives
Endpoint comparisons use the largest common realized-cost checkpoint without interpolation
Every seed, parser failure, support failure, and negative result is retained
